clue.text: Book displayed in window — one recently delivered

indicators.note: a book shown in a window sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a bay is a projecting window

explanation.surface: A book is put on show in a shop window, the latest delivery to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn infant has just been delivered by the midwife.

clue.text: Suffer restlessness without wife? That's charming

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the restless phrase wraps around the wife

parts.note: to suffer restlessness is to be itching

explanation.surface: Someone fidgets when their wife is away, and finds that quite delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means 'outside': W goes inside BE ITCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enchanting casts a spell, which is the sense of bewitching.

clue.text: Intimate report about son

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the loud noise goes round the son

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, a boom

explanation.surface: A confidential account concerning someone's son.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosom friend is a very close, intimate one.

clue.text: Cleric — one runs church, with another holding firm

parts.note: A is one, as in a single item
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: one cleric holding something means it is put inside his title

parts.note: another cleric, here a dean
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: One priest manages the church while another keeps a tight grip on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another cleric, a DEAN, which holds CO.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican clergyman below a bishop.

clue.text: Climbed on parts of roof to get fruit

parts.note: climbed means rose
hips are the sloping edges where roof planes meet

explanation.surface: Someone scaled sections of a roof to pick fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' just places ROSE above HIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosehips are the red seed pods of roses, eaten as a berry-like crop.

clue.text: A singular way to support husband that's faithful

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit below the one they hold up

parts.note: a single thing is one
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A unique way of backing up one's husband that shows loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest and faithful both describe someone true and trustworthy.

clue.text: Bigmouth's speech?

parts.note: a big mouth can be a river's wide mouth, so this is the talk of a river mouth area, the Thames region

explanation.surface: What a loudmouth says.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bigmouth' here is the wide mouth of the Thames; the accent of that area of south-east England is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the accent of London and the Thames mouth region, a mix of Cockney and standard speech.

clue.text: Facial feature of an amorous dart thrower

definitions.text: Facial feature of an amorous dart thrower

parts.words: Facial feature of an amorous dart thrower
parts.note: the curve of the upper lip is named after the weapon the god of love fires arrows from

explanation.surface: A face detail belonging to the god of love with his arrows.
explanation.walkthrough: Cupid fires love-darts from a bow; the double curve of the upper lip is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The double curve of the top lip resembles an archer's weapon, hence the name.

clue.text: Prying boy turned up one of 20

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a boy is a son
20 across is UNKNOWNS; in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so y is one

explanation.surface: A nosy lad looks upward at one of twenty things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses SON to NOS; Y is an algebraic unknown, one of the 20-across entries.
explanation.definitionFit: A prying person pokes into others' business.

clue.text: Ticket-punch or stamp, perhaps?

parts.note: a ticket collector's punch and a stamp collector's stamp are each a thing a collector has or keeps

explanation.surface: Examples of office tools for punching or stamping.
explanation.walkthrough: A ticket collector uses a punch; a stamp is what philatelists collect.
explanation.definitionFit: A prized piece sought by enthusiasts who amass such things.

clue.text: Is joining the right party in victory for state

indicators.note: in places the joined pieces inside the word for victory

parts.note: a victory is a win
CONS is short for Conservatives, the right-wing party

explanation.surface: Being part of the right-wing party in a winning election for the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is a US state in the Midwest.

clue.text: Pieces of pasta rearranged for snack in Spain

indicators.note: rearranged means the letters of pasta are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Bits of pasta shuffled about to make a Spanish snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small savoury dishes served in Spanish bars.

clue.text: Language maiden acquired in the end

indicators.note: the tail acquires, taking in, the maiden letter

parts.note: the end is the tail
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl eventually picked up a new language.
explanation.walkthrough: M for maiden is from cricket scoring, where a maiden is an over with no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian tongue of southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Men in tough US band survived

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Musicians in a hard-bitten American group lived through it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbands are married men.

clue.text: Physicist who was a man of principle? Certainly not!

definitions.text: Physicist who was a man of principle? Certainly not!

parts.words: Physicist who was a man of principle? Certainly not!
parts.note: the scientist is known for a principle whose name is the opposite of certainty

explanation.surface: Was the scientist a principled man? Absolutely not!
explanation.walkthrough: The German physicist formulated the uncertainty principle, so he was a man of the principle of 'certainly not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Werner Heisenberg was the German physicist behind quantum uncertainty.

clue.text: Record on paper novelist's written about policeman

indicators.note: the novelist's name is written around, enclosing, the policeman

parts.note: Thomas Hardy was an English novelist
a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: A novelist has written a book about a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed version of a document, as opposed to an electronic one.

clue.text: An admirable person, for example

parts.note: someone worth admiring sets an example for others to follow

explanation.surface: A person who deserves admiration, say.
explanation.walkthrough: One reading is a pattern to copy; another nods to The Admirable Crichton, a play in which the butler is a stage part.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose conduct others copy is a figure to emulate.

clue.text: A couple of extras said to be leaving?

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the word is written twice

parts.note: a bye is an extra in cricket, a run scored without the bat touching the ball

explanation.surface: Two film extras say farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: A bye is a cricket extra: a run conceded when the ball passes the batter and keeper untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a casual farewell, spoken on departing.

clue.text: Lots of reformed characters quickly spotted by crossword experts

definitions.text: Lots of reformed characters quickly spotted by crossword experts

parts.words: Lots of reformed characters quickly spotted by crossword experts
parts.note: reformed characters are not ex-criminals but jumbled letters, which seasoned solvers soon see

explanation.surface: Many rehabilitated criminals are swiftly identified by puzzle buffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed characters' suggests ex-convicts; it means rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Words formed by rearranging another word's letters are a staple of cryptic clues.

clue.text: Admiral in the hold

definitions.meaning: Horatio ..., the British admiral who won at Trafalgar
a wrestling hold with the arm under the opponent's and the hand on the neck

explanation.surface: A naval officer locked in the ship's cargo space.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves Britain's most famous naval commander and a grip used in wrestling.

clue.text: Such undistinguished people, the last characters listed?

definitions.meaning: obscure people nobody has heard of
x, y and z, the last letters of the alphabet, stand for unknown quantities in algebra

explanation.surface: Ordinary nobodies at the bottom of the cast list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like cast members; it means letters, and x, y, z are algebra's unknown quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure, unfamiliar figures are nobodies; x, y and z mark unsolved values in an equation.

clue.text: Record US entry for field event

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

explanation.surface: An American record entered in an athletics competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the heavy plate is an athletics field event.

clue.text: Powerfully hitting shot in court — ace

definitions.meaning: in tennis, hitting a smash is striking the ball hard overhead
ace as an adjective means excellent, first-rate

explanation.surface: A thunderous tennis stroke that wins a point outright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ace' looks like a tennis serve; here it means splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard overhead tennis stroke is a smash, and British slang uses the same word for wonderful.

clue.text: Compare learner and one with understanding

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
I is the Roman numeral one
ken means understanding or knowledge

explanation.surface: Weigh a student alongside someone who grasps things.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken two things is to draw a comparison between them.

clue.text: Singer raised outside a village

indicators.note: the bird sits outside the single letter, enclosing it
in a down clue raised means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A vocalist brought up on the edge of a village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses LARK to KRAL, which goes outside A.
explanation.definitionFit: A kraal is a traditional southern African village of huts.

clue.text: Beef or fish

explanation.surface: Choosing between meat and seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is to grumble, as to nag or cavil; a freshwater fish shares the name.

clue.text: Some fraud I traced in such a check?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An accountant tracks down fraud during an inspection of the books.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'in', but 'in such a check' cannot stand for a noun; 'in' is a link and 'such a check' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of accounts, where fraud is uncovered.

clue.text: Rating has officer as fellow-student

parts.note: a rating is a grade or class
a mate is a ship's officer

explanation.surface: A naval rating and an officer are fellow students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' looks like a sailor; here it means a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the same school year or group is a fellow pupil.

clue.text: Simple changes in previous manuscript covering earlier text

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged word inside the word for previous

parts.note: past means previous

indicators.note: changes means the letters of simple are rearranged

explanation.surface: Simple edits made to an old manuscript written over an earlier one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges SIMPLE to LIMPSE, which goes inside PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a parchment reused after scraping, with older writing still faintly visible.

clue.text: Beat in return game

indicators.note: in return means the word comes back, read backwards

parts.note: golf is a game

explanation.surface: Win a return match in a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to thrash or whip.
